**Top‑populated Santa Rosa County cities whose median owner‑occupied‑home value (2019‑2023 ACS 5‑year estimate) was **above $200 k** – listed from highest to lowest**

| Rank | City | Median value of owner‑occupied housing units (2019‑2023) |

| 2 | **Navarre** | **$375,700** ± $11,871 (ACS 5‑year, B25077) – *Data USA* |
| 3 | **Pace** | **$293,800** ± $16,581 (ACS 5‑year, B25077) – *Data USA* |

## What are Santa Rosa County, FL's racial and ethnic demographics?
Non-Hispanic white residents make up 79.5% of the Santa Rosa County, FL population, higher than the national share of 57.5%. Santa Rosa County also has a larger share of people identifying as non-Hispanic two or more races (3.5%) than the US overall (2.5%).
In contrast, Santa Rosa County’s Hispanic population accounts for 7.4%, below the 20% nationwide, and the non-Hispanic Black or African American population makes up 6.3% of the county, compared with 12.6% nationally.
Racial and ethnic make up differ based on location. These figures reflect how people identified their race alone (not in combination with other races), and separate out Hispanic or Latino ethnicity, following Census reporting standards.
Santa Rosa County, FL has a higher share of a non-Hispanic white population than Florida as a whole.

Title: Santa Rosa County's population soars above 200,000 for first time; Pensacola drops
Chunks: 0
May 22, 2024, 4:25 a.m. CT
When Sam Parker was elected county commissioner for the first time in 2016, the number of people residing in Santa Rosa County stood at just over 170,000.
Today, as Parker seeks his third term in office, the US Census Bureau is reporting that for the first time Santa Rosa County's population has eclipsed the 200,000 mark, and as of July 1, 2023 stood at 203,162.

**Santa Rosa County** is a county in the northwestern portion of the U.S. state of Florida. As of 2020, its population was 188,000. The county seat is Milton, which lies in the geographic center of the county. Other major communities within Santa Rosa County are Navarre, Pace, and Gulf Breeze.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Santa_Rosa_County,_Florida#cite_note-GR6-1) Navarre is the most populated community, with a population of approximately 45,000 residents. Santa Rosa County is included in the Pensacola metropolitan area, which also includes Escambia County.

The first European in Santa Rosa County may have been Diego Maldonado, a member of Tristan de Luna's failed expedition. Natives dominated the area until the late 1700s. A Spanish mission serving Apalachees, Nuestra Señora de la Soledad y San Luís, may have been located in Floridatown from 1718 until 1740.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Santa_Rosa_County,_Florida#cite_note-2)[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Santa_Rosa_County,_Florida#cite_note-3)
Santa Rosa County was created in 1842, when it was divided from Escambia County. It was named after the barrier island along its southern coast, which, in turn, had been named for the Roman Catholic saint Rosa de Viterbo.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Santa_Rosa_County,_Florida#cite_note-4)
Santa Rosa County repealed its prohibition on alcohol in 2005.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Santa_Rosa_County,_Florida#cite_note-5)
Santa Rosa County has seen unprecedented growth in population, specifically in Navarre, Pace, and Gulf Breeze. The county is a quickly growing tourist destination because of its access to beaches and protected wilderness areas for kayaking, hiking, and camping.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Santa_Rosa_County,_Florida#cite_note-6)
According to the U.S. Census Bureau, the county has a total area of 1,174 square miles (3,040 km 2), of which 162 sq mi (420 km 2) (13.8%) are covered by water.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Santa_Rosa_County,_Florida#cite_note-GR1-7)

### National protected area
[edit]
*   Choctawhatchee National Forest (part)
Santa Rosa County can be divided into three distinct sections: South Santa Rosa, Central Santa Rosa, and North Santa Rosa. The sections are centered on the main east–west roads that pass through the county.
Navarre Beach
South Santa Rosa County comprises the area from Holley and Navarre in the east to Gulf Breeze]at the western end of the Fairpoint Peninsula, and along U.S. Highway 98. A section of Santa Rosa Island, containing the unincorporated community of Navarre Beach, is also part of South Santa Rosa County. Major bodies of water including Santa Rosa Sound, Pensacola Bay, and East Bay strongly influence the housing and lifestyle of citizens in the southern part of the county. This fast-growing region serves primarily as "bedroom communities" for Pensacola to the west and Hurlburt Field, Fort Walton Beach, and Eglin Air Force Base to the east.
Central Santa Rosa County is the area north of the bays and south of the extensive forests separating it from North Santa Rosa. The central section developed along the so-called Old Spanish Trail that ran from St. Augustine to New Orleans, and further points west. Today, U.S. Highway 90 closely parallels the old trail, and is the main highway that connects the region. Despite recent growth, the Central Region is best identified by its rural roots, and can be best characterized by traditional Southern culture. The Pace and Milton communities compose the Central Region, with both having populations roughly around 30,000.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Santa_Rosa_County,_Florida#cite_note-8)[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Santa_Rosa_County,_Florida#cite_note-9) The county seat, Milton is located where the trail crossed the Blackwater River. To the west of Milton bordering the Escambia River, Pace has experienced exponential growth, both residential and commercial. Interstate 10 also passes through this section of the county. The U.S. Navy presence is marked by Whiting Field and NOLF Spencer Field.

### National protected area
Northern Santa Rosa County is forest and farming country. The only town in the north is Jay. Most development has been along State Road 4, which runs through the northern sections of Escambia, Santa Rosa, and Okaloosa Counties. A large oil and natural gas field around Jay produced a great deal of oil, and made many farmers millionaires in the 1970s and 1980s, but the field has been depleted and is producing little oil today. The citizens have, for the most part, returned to farming and forestry for their livelihoods.
State Road 87 traverses the county from north to south, between U.S. Highway 98 and the border with Escambia County, Alabama, near Brewton, where it connects with State Route 41. This road is a primary emergency evacuation route for the county during hurricanes.

### Racial and ethnic composition
The racial makeup of the county was 80.4% White, 5.9% Black or African American, 0.7% American Indian and Alaska Native, 2.1% Asian, 0.2% Native Hawaiian and Pacific Islander, 1.9% from some other race, and 8.8% from two or more races. Hispanic or Latino residents of any race comprised 6.3% of the population.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Santa_Rosa_County,_Florida#cite_note-Census2020PL-26)
80.1% of residents lived in urban areas, while 19.9% lived in rural areas.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Santa_Rosa_County,_Florida#cite_note-Census2020DHC-27)
Of the 69,454 households, 32.8% had children under the age of 18 living in them; 56.6% were married-couple households, 15.2% were households with a male householder and no spouse or partner present, and 22.1% were households with a female householder and no spouse or partner present. About 21.5% of all households were made up of individuals and 9.6% had someone living alone who was 65 years of age or older.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Santa_Rosa_County,_Florida#cite_note-Census2020DP-25)
There were 75,854 housing units, of which 8.4% were vacant. Among occupied housing units, 77.3% were owner-occupied and 22.7% were renter-occupied. The homeowner vacancy rate was 1.4% and the rental vacancy rate was 8.5%.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Santa_Rosa_County,_Florida#cite_note-Census2020DP-25)

### Racial and ethnic composition
As of the 2000 census,[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Santa_Rosa_County,_Florida#cite_note-GR8-28) 117,743 people, 43,793 households, and 33,326 families resided in the county. The population density was 116 inhabitants per square mile (45/km 2). The 49,119 housing units had an average density of 48 per square mile (19/km 2). The racial makeup of the county was 90.72% White, 4.25% African American, 1.01% Native American, 1.30% Asian, 0.08% Pacific Islander, 0.67% from other races, and 1.98% from two or more races. About 2.52% of the population were Hispanics or Latinos of any race.
Of the 43,793 households, 36.5% had children under 18 living with them, 62.2% were married couples living together, 10.2% had a female householder with no husband present, and 23.9% were not families. About 19.3% of all households were made up of individuals, and 6.6% had someone living alone who was 65 or older. The average household size was 2.63 and the average family size was 3.00.
In the county, the age distribution was 26.6% under 18, 7.2% from 18 to 24, 31.1% from 25 to 44, 24.1% from 45 to 64, and 11.0% who were 65 or older. The median age was 37 years. For every 100 females, there were 100.6 males. For every 100 females 18 and over, there were 97.9 males.

### Racial and ethnic composition
The median income for a household in the county was $41,881 and for a family was $46,929. Males had a median income of $34,878 versus $22,304 for females. The per capita income for the county was $20,089. About 7.9% of families and 9.8% of the population were below the poverty line, including 12.6% of those under 18 and 7.5% of those 65 or over.
The Santa Rosa County Library System has five branches located in: Navarre, Gulf Breeze, Jay, Milton, and Pace.

**Navarre** has grown from being a small town of around 1,500 in 1970 to a town with a population estimated at 41,490 as of 2020. Navarre is an unincorporated community in Santa Rosa County in the Northwest Florida Panhandle. Home to Navarre Beach as well as several miles of beaches within the Navarre Marine Beach Park and the Gulf National Islands Seashore, Navarre is a rapidly growing coastal community of nature enthusiasts, families, and retirees.
**Gulf Breeze** is a city in Santa Rosa County and is a suburb of Pensacola. In 2020, the census reported a population of 6,900. In 1828, the US Government purchased the land encompassing the Naval Live Oaks Reservation for experimenting with acorns for the cultivation of live oaks to produce wooden ships. The Naval Live Oaks Reservation is now part of the Gulf Islands National Seashore.

## History of Santa Rosa County
The first European to visit Santa Rosa County might have been Diego Maldonado. He was part of an expedition led by Tristan de Luna. Native American groups lived here for a long time, until the late 1700s. A Spanish mission (a type of church settlement) for the Apalachee people might have been in Floridatown from 1718 to 1740.
Santa Rosa County was officially created in 1842. It was formed from a part of Escambia County. The county got its name from a nearby island, which was named after a Catholic saint, Rosa de Viterbo.
In 2005, Santa Rosa County changed a rule that had stopped people from buying alcohol.
The county has grown a lot, especially in Navarre, Pace, and Gulf Breeze. Many tourists now visit Santa Rosa County. They come for the beautiful beaches and protected natural areas. These areas are great for kayaking, hiking, and camping.

## Geography and Natural Areas
Santa Rosa County covers about 1,174 square miles. Most of this area, about 1,012 square miles, is land. The rest, about 162 square miles, is water.

## Geography and Natural Areas
### National Protected Lands
*   Choctawhatchee National Forest (part of it is in Santa Rosa County)

## Geography and Natural Areas
### Different Regions of the County
Santa Rosa County can be split into three main parts: South Santa Rosa, Central Santa Rosa, and North Santa Rosa. These areas are named after the main roads that cross the county from east to west.

## Geography and Natural Areas
### Different Regions of the County
#### South Santa Rosa County
This area stretches from Holley and Navarre in the east to Gulf Breeze in the west. It follows U.S. Highway 98. A part of Santa Rosa Island, which includes Navarre Beach, is also in South Santa Rosa County. Large bodies of water like Santa Rosa Sound, Pensacola Bay, and East Bay are very important here. They affect how people live and what kinds of homes are built. This area is growing fast. Many people live here and travel to Pensacola for work. Others work at military bases like Hurlburt Field and Eglin Air Force Base.

## Geography and Natural Areas
### Different Regions of the County
#### Central Santa Rosa County
This part of the county is north of the bays and south of the large forests. It grew up along an old road called the Old Spanish Trail. Today, U.S. Highway 90 follows this old trail. It is the main road connecting this region. Even with recent growth, Central Santa Rosa County still feels very rural. It has a traditional Southern culture. The communities of Pace and Milton are in this region. Both have populations of about 30,000 people. Milton, the county seat, is where the old trail crossed the Blackwater River. To the west of Milton, Pace has grown a lot with new homes and businesses. Interstate 10 also goes through this area. The U.S. Navy has a presence here with Whiting Field and NOLF Spencer Field.

## Geography and Natural Areas
### Different Regions of the County
#### North Santa Rosa County
This area is mostly forests and farms. The only town in the north is Jay. Most development has happened along State Road 4. This road goes through the northern parts of Escambia, Santa Rosa, and Okaloosa counties. In the 1970s and 1980s, a large oil and natural gas field near Jay made many farmers very rich. However, most of the oil is gone now. People in this area have mostly gone back to farming and working in forestry.
State Road 87 runs through the county from north to south. It connects U.S. Highway 98 to the border with Escambia County, Alabama near Brewton. This road is very important for people to leave the county safely during hurricanes.

## Geography and Natural Areas
### Neighboring Counties
*   Escambia County, Alabama - to the north  
*   Okaloosa County, Florida - to the east  
*   Escambia County, Florida - to the west

**Santa Rosa County** is a county in the northwestern portion of the U.S. state of Florida. As of 2020, its population was 188,000. The county seat is Milton, which lies in the geographic center of the county. Other major communities within Santa Rosa County are Navarre, Pace, and Gulf Breeze.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Santa_Rosa_County,_Florida#cite_note-GR6-1) Navarre is the most populated community, with a population of approximately 45,000 residents. Santa Rosa County is included in the Pensacola metropolitan area, which also includes Escambia County.

The first European in Santa Rosa County may have been Diego Maldonado, a member of Tristan de Luna's failed expedition. Natives dominated the area until the late 1700s. A Spanish mission serving Apalachees, Nuestra Señora de la Soledad y San Luís, may have been located in Floridatown from 1718 until 1740.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Santa_Rosa_County,_Florida#cite_note-2)[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Santa_Rosa_County,_Florida#cite_note-3)
Santa Rosa County was created in 1842, when it was divided from Escambia County. It was named after the barrier island along its southern coast, which, in turn, had been named for the Roman Catholic saint Rosa de Viterbo.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Santa_Rosa_County,_Florida#cite_note-4)
Santa Rosa County repealed its prohibition on alcohol in 2005.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Santa_Rosa_County,_Florida#cite_note-5)
Santa Rosa County has seen unprecedented growth in population, specifically in Navarre, Pace, and Gulf Breeze. The county is a quickly growing tourist destination because of its access to beaches and protected wilderness areas for kayaking, hiking, and camping.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Santa_Rosa_County,_Florida#cite_note-6)
According to the U.S. Census Bureau, the county has a total area of 1,174 square miles (3,040 km 2), of which 162 sq mi (420 km 2) (13.8%) are covered by water.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Santa_Rosa_County,_Florida#cite_note-GR1-7)

As of the 2000 census,[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Santa_Rosa_County,_Florida#cite_note-GR8-28) 117,743 people, 43,793 households, and 33,326 families resided in the county. The racial makeup of the county was 90.72% White, 4.25% African American, 1.01% Native American, 1.30% Asian, 0.08% Pacific Islander, 0.67% from other races, and 1.98% from two or more races. About 2.52% of the population were Hispanics or Latinos of any race.
Of the 43,793 households, 36.5% had children under 18 living with them, 62.2% were married couples living together, 10.2% had a female householder with no husband present, and 23.9% were not families. About 19.3% of all households were made up of individuals, and 6.6% had someone living alone who was 65 or older. The average household size was 2.63 and the average family size was 3.00.
In the county, the age distribution was 26.6% under 18, 7.2% from 18 to 24, 31.1% from 25 to 44, 24.1% from 45 to 64, and 11.0% who were 65 or older. The median age was 37 years. For every 100 females, there were 100.6 males. For every 100 females 18 and over, there were 97.9 males.

Other important communities in Santa Rosa County include Navarre, Pace, and Gulf Breeze. Navarre is the biggest community, with around 45,000 people. Santa Rosa County is part of a larger city area called the Pensacola Metropolitan Statistical Area. This area also includes Escambia County.

## History of Santa Rosa County
The first European to visit Santa Rosa County might have been Diego Maldonado. He was part of an expedition led by Tristan de Luna. Native American groups lived here for a long time, until the late 1700s. A Spanish mission (a type of church settlement) for the Apalachee people might have been in Floridatown from 1718 to 1740.
Santa Rosa County was officially created in 1842. It was formed from a part of Escambia County. The county got its name from a nearby island, which was named after a Catholic saint, Rosa de Viterbo.
In 2005, Santa Rosa County changed a rule that had stopped people from buying alcohol.
The county has grown a lot, especially in Navarre, Pace, and Gulf Breeze. Many tourists now visit Santa Rosa County. They come for the beautiful beaches and protected natural areas. These areas are great for kayaking, hiking, and camping.

## Geography and Natural Areas
Santa Rosa County covers about 1,174 square miles. Most of this area, about 1,012 square miles, is land. The rest, about 162 square miles, is water.

## Geography and Natural Areas
### National Protected Lands
*   Choctawhatchee National Forest (part of it is in Santa Rosa County)

## Geography and Natural Areas
### Different Regions of the County
Santa Rosa County can be split into three main parts: South Santa Rosa, Central Santa Rosa, and North Santa Rosa. These areas are named after the main roads that cross the county from east to west.

## Geography and Natural Areas
### Different Regions of the County
#### South Santa Rosa County
This area stretches from Holley and Navarre in the east to Gulf Breeze in the west. It follows U.S. Highway 98. A part of Santa Rosa Island, which includes Navarre Beach, is also in South Santa Rosa County. Large bodies of water like Santa Rosa Sound, Pensacola Bay, and East Bay are very important here. They affect how people live and what kinds of homes are built. This area is growing fast. Many people live here and travel to Pensacola for work. Others work at military bases like Hurlburt Field and Eglin Air Force Base.

## Geography and Natural Areas
### Different Regions of the County
#### Central Santa Rosa County
This part of the county is north of the bays and south of the large forests. It grew up along an old road called the Old Spanish Trail. Today, U.S. Highway 90 follows this old trail. It is the main road connecting this region. Even with recent growth, Central Santa Rosa County still feels very rural. It has a traditional Southern culture. The communities of Pace and Milton are in this region. Both have populations of about 30,000 people. Milton, the county seat, is where the old trail crossed the Blackwater River. To the west of Milton, Pace has grown a lot with new homes and businesses. Interstate 10 also goes through this area. The U.S. Navy has a presence here with Whiting Field and NOLF Spencer Field.

## Geography and Natural Areas
### Different Regions of the County
#### North Santa Rosa County
This area is mostly forests and farms. The only town in the north is Jay. Most development has happened along State Road 4. This road goes through the northern parts of Escambia, Santa Rosa, and Okaloosa counties. In the 1970s and 1980s, a large oil and natural gas field near Jay made many farmers very rich. However, most of the oil is gone now. People in this area have mostly gone back to farming and working in forestry.
State Road 87 runs through the county from north to south. It connects U.S. Highway 98 to the border with Escambia County, Alabama near Brewton. This road is very important for people to leave the county safely during hurricanes.

## Geography and Natural Areas
### Neighboring Counties
*   Escambia County, Alabama - to the north  
*   Okaloosa County, Florida - to the east  
*   Escambia County, Florida - to the west

In the county, the age distribution was 26.6% under 18, 7.2% from 18 to 24, 31.1% from 25 to 44, 24.1% from 45 to 64, and 11.0% who were 65 or older. The median age was 37 years. For every 100 females, there were 100.6 males. For every 100 females 18 and over, there were 97.9 males.

Resideline Team
If you invest in or around Navarre, the number that matters is what homes actually close for, not what sellers are asking. Here is what Navarre sale prices look like right now, built from the closings Resideline tracked over the last six months, as of October 2026.

## The snapshot
*   •**Closings tracked, last 6 months:** 507

## What the numbers say
Resideline tracked 507 closed sales in Navarre over the last six months, with a median closing price of $415,000. That median is the midpoint of what buyers actually paid, not what sellers hoped to get, which is why it moves differently from the asking prices you see on listing sites. The middle half of those sales closed between $327,000 and $512,000. That spread matters more than the headline median: where a specific property sits inside it decides whether the citywide number helps you or misleads you. These are the closings Resideline tracks and may differ from complete county or municipal records. 88% of the Navarre closings we track here are single-family houses, so these figures primarily reflect that segment, and the citywide $/sqft figure primarily reflects that segment as well. Across the 504 closings with usable living area, the middle half sold between $196 and $238 per square foot.

## What the numbers say
Resideline tracked 507 closed sales in Navarre over the last six months, with a median closing price of $415,000. That median is the midpoint of what buyers actually paid, not what sellers hoped to get, which is why it moves differently from the asking prices you see on listing sites. The middle half of those sales closed between $327,000 and $512,000. That spread matters more than the headline median: where a specific property sits inside it decides whether the citywide number helps you or misleads you. These are the closings Resideline tracks and may differ from complete county or municipal records. 88% of the Navarre closings we track here are single-family houses, so these figures primarily reflect that segment, and the citywide $/sqft figure primarily reflects that segment as well. Across the 504 closings with usable living area, the middle half sold between $196 and $238 per square foot.

Editorial Standards ⓘ
By Annie Jennemann
**WASHINGTON —**  
Home values are up across the U.S., according to new estimates released by the U.S. Census Bureau.
The value of owner-occupied homes rose by 21.7% for survey data collected between 2019 and 2023 as compared to data collected from 2014 to 2018, according to a release from the bureau. The nationwide rise accounts for inflation.
Advertisement
The data released Thursday are American Community Survey five-year estimates calculated using a pool of data between 2019 and 2023. The five-year estimates, unlike the annual data released by the bureau which covers larger populations, cover all population sizes in smaller geographic areas.
The estimates also show a decline in the median share of income homeowners pay toward housing costs, according to the release. The median for data collected between 2014 and 2018 was 18.3% and shrank to 17.5% in this year’s estimates. Owner-occupied housing units increased by 8.4% from the prior survey period from 2014 to 2018, according to the release.
Almost all counties saw some increase in median home value. Both sets of data are adjusted for inflation for the final year of the time period.
Out of 3,144 counties in the U.S., just over 15% had a median home value for owned units larger than the $303,400 nationwide median.

## Housing Units and Costs
### Selected Monthly and Annual Owner Costs
Homeowners with and without mortgages have ongoing monthly costs, and the American Community Survey gathers data about these costs, which are reported in tables referring to "selected monthly owner costs." The costs are reported as either a percentage of the household income or the number of housing units in a monthly cost range such as “$1,250 to $1,499”. The selected costs used for these estimates are:
*   payments for mortgages, or other debts on the property  
*   real estate taxes  
*   fire, hazard, and flood insurance  
*   utilities (electricity, gas, and water and sewer)

Editorial Standards ⓘ
By Annie Jennemann
**WASHINGTON —**  
Home values are up across the U.S., according to new estimates released by the U.S. Census Bureau.
The value of owner-occupied homes rose by 21.7% for survey data collected between 2019 and 2023 as compared to data collected from 2014 to 2018, according to a release from the bureau. The nationwide rise accounts for inflation.
Advertisement
The data released Thursday are American Community Survey five-year estimates calculated using a pool of data between 2019 and 2023. The five-year estimates, unlike the annual data released by the bureau which covers larger populations, cover all population sizes in smaller geographic areas.
The estimates also show a decline in the median share of income homeowners pay toward housing costs, according to the release. The median for data collected between 2014 and 2018 was 18.3% and shrank to 17.5% in this year’s estimates. Owner-occupied housing units increased by 8.4% from the prior survey period from 2014 to 2018, according to the release.
Almost all counties saw some increase in median home value. Both sets of data are adjusted for inflation for the final year of the time period.
Out of 3,144 counties in the U.S., just over 15% had a median home value for owned units larger than the $303,400 nationwide median.
View the map below to see the median value for owner-occupied homes for the estimates calculated between 2019 and 2023.

By Annie Jennemann
**WASHINGTON —**  
Home values are up across the U.S., according to new estimates released by the U.S. Census Bureau.
The value of owner-occupied homes rose by 21.7% for survey data collected between 2019 and 2023 as compared to data collected from 2014 to 2018, according to a release from the bureau. The nationwide rise accounts for inflation.
Advertisement
The data released Thursday are American Community Survey five-year estimates calculated using a pool of data between 2019 and 2023. The five-year estimates, unlike the annual data released by the bureau which covers larger populations, cover all population sizes in smaller geographic areas.
The estimates also show a decline in the median share of income homeowners pay toward housing costs, according to the release. The median for data collected between 2014 and 2018 was 18.3% and shrank to 17.5% in this year’s estimates. Owner-occupied housing units increased by 8.4% from the prior survey period from 2014 to 2018, according to the release.
Almost all counties saw some increase in median home value. Both sets of data are adjusted for inflation for the final year of the time period.
Out of 3,144 counties in the U.S., just over 15% had a median home value for owned units larger than the $303,400 nationwide median.
